newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ILL CZECH PRESIDENT HAVEL CANCELS NOVEMBER PLANS.
newsitem.headline: ILL CZECH PRESIDENT HAVEL CANCELS NOVEMBER PLANS.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel cancelled a two-day state visit to Ukraine, planned to start on Tuesday, because he is suffering from pneumonia, his office said on Monday.
The president's spokesman, Ladislav Spacek, said in a statement that Havel also cancelled the rest of his scheduled programme for the rest of November due to his condition.
"Because of the illness the state visit to Ukraine is being postponed and the rest of (Havel's) working programme for two weeks is cancelled," the statement said.
It said Havel had not been in hospital.

The illness caused the president to forego his tradition of laying anniversary flowers at a monument on Prague's National Avenue (Narodni Trida) where the Havel-led velvet revolution over the Communist government began seven years ago on Sunday.
During the visit to Kiev and points elsewhere, Havel was to meet Ukraine's president Leonid Kuchma, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, and see the Chernobyl nuclear power plant.
